Questions & answers.

Lykeion is a scientific control plane for human scientists and AI agents, connecting literature grounding, hypothesis formation, experimentation, validation, and reporting.

Lykeion (Λύκειον) is the Greek name of the Lyceum, Aristotle’s school in ancient Athens. It reflects a commitment to observation, inquiry, and evidence.

Scientists set the research agenda, define boundaries and budgets, and intervene when their judgment is needed. Lykeion’s ambition is to reduce routine step-by-step verification through coordinated research workflows.

Individual tools can retrieve papers, write code, or draft text. Lykeion connects those activities through a scientific workflow where evidence and criticism can send an inquiry back to an earlier stage.

A contradiction should prompt a revised hypothesis or another experiment. A negative finding should remain part of the research record, rather than disappear from the report.

Read About Lykeion for its mission and the AutoResearch survey informing the project, or explore the documentation.

Make room for discovery.

Network content is retained only when selected; response bytes are browser-decoded, not compressed wire bytes.
Request bytes are limited to what Playwright exposes; not_exposed does not establish body absence or multipart file coverage.
Network content reads settle within 5 seconds each and never wait for unfinished responses or refetch them.
Playwright scenario events do not expose request initiator stacks; receipt order does not prove causality.
Storage values are hashed only after declared-secret redaction.
